contract: Surface temperature = meanCelsius + beltAmplitudeCelsius * cos(2 pi z / beltPeriodBlocks) + noiseAmplitudeCelsius * (broad + detailWeight * detail) / (1 + detailWeight), with broad noise at scaleBlocks and detail at scaleBlocks * detailScaleFraction, both on domain-warped coordinates that ClimateMap shares. A belt period of 0 disables the belt.

Background moisture = 0.5 + 0.5 * (broad + detailWeight * detail) / (1 + detailWeight) + beltAmplitude * cos(2 pi (x + beltOffsetBlocks) / beltPeriodBlocks), clamped to 0..1, on the same warped coordinates, broad at broadBlocks and detail at detailBlocks, before upwind forcing (riven-climate-forcing.json). The moisture belt runs east-west, across the temperature belt, so every climate band spans dry to wet; a belt period of 0 disables it.
Temperature reads no altitude, plates, water or biome; later layers consume it.

Tuned for 8 km worlds (32 km maximum): a 16 km belt with the origin on the mean gives every 8 km world half a cycle and a 32 km world two cycles; target blend about 20% cold (FROZEN), 60% temperate (COOL, MILD, WARM), 20% hot (HOT). Moisture (climate-v3): features at 2,000 and 800 blocks give an 8 km world several wet and dry lobes, and the belt (wet west, dry east, half a cycle per 8 km world) keeps them from lining up with the temperature bands; over six seeds dry land (riven-biomes.json cores) is 16-31% and forest climates 50-75%.
